references.text: The Lord said to Abram: Go from your country, from your kindred and from your father's house, to the land that I will show you.
For all the land that you see, I will give it to you and to your offspring forever.
Get up, walk through the land in every direction! For I will give it to you.
He brought him outside and said: Look up toward the sky, and count the stars, if you are able to count them. And he said to him: So numerous shall your offspring be.

Your offspring shall be like the dust of the earth, and you shall spread out to the west and to the east, to the north and to the south. In you and in your offspring all the families of the earth shall be blessed.
Go up to the top of Pisgah and lift up your eyes toward the west and the north, toward the south and the east, and look out with your eyes. For you shall not cross over the Jordan.
Explains the historical reason why Abram was invited to look out over the land: the decision to separate from Lot.
Shows God's pattern of confirming promises and giving comfort to Abram immediately after critical life events.
Connects the original promise of the land to Abraham (13:14) with God's sworn commitment to give this land to his descendants (Deut 33:1).
